name: Scheat
description: A star 60 parsecs away, 115 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 113881: radius 114.864 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1863.64 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.071) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 113881: effective temperature 3541 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.088)

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 113881: RV 7.99 +/- 0.23 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 113881: distance 60.096 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 60 parsecs away, 115 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,864 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,541 K, so 114.864 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 113881: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Pegasi
quotes.card: Beta Pegasi, formally named Scheat, is a red giant star and the second-brightest star in the constellation of Pegasus.
quotes.introduction: It forms the upper right corner of the Great Square of Pegasus, a prominent rectangular asterism.
